title: woodsia glabella subsp. asplenioides
intro: Woodsia glabella subsp. asplenioides, commonly known as the asplenioid woodsia fern, is a species of fern in the family Woodsiaceae. It is a type of vascular plant that belongs to the division Pteridophyta, characterized by its small, delicate fronds and ability to thrive in shaded, moist environments. The asplenioid woodsia fern has been traditionally used in folk medicine to treat various health issues, including fever, rheumatism, and digestive problems, due to its therapeutic actions as an anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial, and antiseptic agent. The bioactive constituents of this plant include flavonoids, saponins, and terpenoids, which contribute to its potential health benefits and medicinal properties.
